episode_title: German Road Logistics: LIT Buys Duvenbeck

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Two German road hauliers are becoming one, with about ten thousand four hundred people and more than a hundred and eighty sites.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: The prize is automotive logistics, and this is The Planning Desk.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Good morning, it's Monday the second of November, and I'm Anna.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: And I'm Erik.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Quick note, this show is made with A I. A I agents gather the news, and our voices are synthetic.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: On the desk, a German logistics merger, a six billion dollar warehouse bet from Walmart, Stora Enso holding back on spending, and a memory chip squeeze that runs to twenty twenty-eight.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: On Friday the L I T Group of Brake, in Lower Saxony, signed to buy all shares in Duvenbeck, the road logistics group from Bocholt, from Waterland Private Equity.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Waterland has held a stake since twenty twenty-two. The price wasn't disclosed, and the deal still needs competition clearance, with closing expected later this year.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Duvenbeck brings about five thousand staff and more than fifty European sites. L I T has about five thousand four hundred staff and more than a hundred and thirty sites in twenty-two countries.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: L I T says it wants to grow in automotive logistics and in southern and eastern Europe, and that Duvenbeck's restructuring will carry on. How the two networks fit together is still open.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: It comes only a week after Boluda agreed to buy Samskip, another European carrier changing hands.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: For automotive shippers and suppliers, expect site and lane consolidation once the deal closes. If you use either carrier, put a capacity and contract review into the twenty twenty-seven transport plan now.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Ask both carriers which sites serve your lanes today, because the integration plan isn't written yet.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: To the U S, where Walmart has expanded its deal with automation supplier Symbotic, with an initial commitment of about six billion dollars over several years.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: That covers twenty-five regional distribution centres, with each-picking, micro-fulfilment for online orders and A I software that coordinates millions of cases a day.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Walmart says it expects better upstream inventory for e-commerce, more storage, a wider range and steadier replenishment, but it gave no start or finish dates.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: When the warehouse runs on software, replenishment can run on tighter and more frequent cycles, so suppliers into those centres should revisit their order-pattern assumptions.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Over to the Nordics, where Stora Enso is spending less and warning on costs.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The packaging group cut this year's capital spending plan to about five hundred million euros, and the lower investment lifted its quarterly cash flow.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: For the fourth quarter it expects demand to stay subdued, while costs for energy, logistics, chemicals and wood rise, according to its interim report.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Consumer packaging was also hit by planned maintenance and lower volumes, and the ramp-up of its Oulu line runs into twenty twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: So weak demand won't mean cheap board. If you buy packaging, plan for firm prices on some grades.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: In Germany, two industrial suppliers cut their outlooks on Friday.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Power supply and drive systems maker FRIWO lowered its forecast again, citing lower call-off volumes from customers and more low-cost competition from Asia, especially in robotic mowers and e-mobility.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: MAX Automation adjusted its guidance too, because its Vecoplan group is behind plan on orders, and restructuring at Vecoplan and N S M plus Jücker costs more.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Falling call-offs against framework orders mean customers are running down stock. If you supply German industry, plan first-quarter production on call-off trends, not order books.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: And memory chips are turning into an allocation market.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: SupplyChainBrain reports a price of up to eighteen hundred dollars is being discussed for Microsoft's next Xbox, Project Helix, though that's far from certain.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Earlier in October, Micron's chief executive said memory demand would exceed supply in both twenty twenty-seven and twenty twenty-eight, with no balance in sight.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: If your bill of materials has D RAM or flash in it, plan twenty twenty-seven on allocated volumes and long-term agreements, not spot buys.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Global sales of mobile warehouse robots rose nineteen percent last year, Industriemagazin reports, and the German engineering association V D M A warns European makers are falling behind Asia.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Brussels has cleared twenty-nine point three million euros of German state aid for a new road and rail freight terminal at Stolberg, near Aachen.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's another intermodal option on the Aachen corridor, useful while low water on the Rhine keeps barges short.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: And October factory surveys for Sweden and Germany are out today, so watch Sweden's inventory and delivery times after September's reading of fifty-eight point one.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: That's the desk for Monday, thanks for starting the week with us.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: We're back tomorrow morning with more.

Germany's L.I.T. Group is buying Duvenbeck, and automotive shippers should expect their lanes to be redrawn.

L.I.T. Group of Brake has signed to buy all shares in Bocholt-based Duvenbeck from Waterland Private Equity. Together they have about 10,400 employees and more than 180 sites, according to eurotransport. Closing is expected later in 2026, subject to competition clearance.

For automotive shippers and suppliers using either carrier, expect site and lane consolidation once the deal closes. Put a carrier-capacity and contract review into the 2027 transport plan now.

Also on today's desk:
Stora Enso cut its 2026 capex to about €500m and expects energy, logistics and wood costs to rise in Q4.
Micron sees memory demand outrunning supply through 2028, so plan DRAM on allocation.

Which of your 2027 lanes run on a carrier that changed owner this year?
